title: Count every unit
summary: Repair an in-memory stock counter with strict validation and unchanged failure state.

constraints: Keep Inventory(stock), available(sku), and reserve(sku, quantity); use an independent copy of the input mapping. Missing SKU returns None from available and False from reserve.
An initial stock mapping has non-empty string SKU keys and exact integer quantities >= 0. Booleans, non-integers, negative quantities and invalid keys raise ValueError.
Reservation quantity must be an exact integer > 0 and SKU a non-empty string; invalid input raises ValueError before any mutation. Whitespace-only SKU is invalid; other SKU text is preserved exactly.

reserve returns True and decrements exactly once if enough stock exists; insufficient or missing stock returns False unchanged. This exercise is single-process in memory; persistence and concurrency are outside its contract.

prerequisites.title: Correctness and boundary tests
prerequisites.description: Be comfortable tracing a branch and writing an assertion for a boundary value.

stages.title: Understand the contract
stages.brief: Repair an in-memory stock counter with strict validation and unchanged failure state. Use Python 3.11 standard-library modules only.

stages.title: Implement the change
stages.brief: Preserve the documented interface and explain your choices.
requirements: Preserve valid behavior and exact request identity.

stages.title: Verify the behavior
stages.brief: Run the authored checks and add one targeted learner regression check.
requirements: Use the disclosed contract and failure cases.
Explain what the observed checks do not establish.

stages.title: Defend your decisions
stages.brief: Explain your code, evidence and remaining limits.
requirements: Cite concrete code or executed checks.
Describe one alternative and its trade-off.

rubric.name: State invariants
rubric.description: Keep accepted quantity plus remaining stock equal to the original count.

anchors.strong: Preserves exact counts for accepted and rejected requests and explains the invariant.
anchors.developing: Common success works but a rejection changes state or count conservation is not explained.
anchors.needsWork: Accepts overspending, negative quantities or state corruption.

rubric.name: Input boundaries
rubric.description: Validate exact types before changing state.

anchors.strong: Rejects booleans and malformed values without mutating caller or internal state.
anchors.developing: Validation handles typical input but misses a disclosed type or ownership boundary.
anchors.needsWork: Treats Python booleans as stock quantities or mutates the input mapping.

rubric.name: Targeted regression evidence
rubric.description: Use a small failing boundary check to support the repair.

anchors.strong: Adds a targeted regression and explains why sequential checks do not establish concurrent safety.
anchors.developing: Runs common success checks without a targeted boundary example.
anchors.needsWork: Claims behavior unsupported by checks or skips verification.

probes.question: Which statement preserves the count invariant on a rejected reservation?
Which inputs can compare like integers while violating this contract?
What does your smallest regression check show, and what remains outside this task?

hints: Write the count invariant for one SKU before editing.
In Python bool is a subclass of int; exact integer validation needs a deliberate choice.
Do not subtract until every precondition has passed, and copy the caller-owned mapping.
